title: Reading files: cat, less, head, tail
summary: Four ways to look inside a file, from a short note to a log that keeps growing.

scheme: cat notes.txt     the whole file, all at once
less big.log      page by page, q to quit
text: - cat is for short files: a long one scrolls past too fast.
- less lets you move around. /word searches, n finds the next one, q quits.
- head shows the start, tail the end (10 lines unless you say -n).
- The newest lines of a log are at the end: tail is the one you'll use most.
tail -f follows the file: it waits and prints each new line as it arrives.
- Perfect to watch a program while you test it. Ctrl+C stops watching.
